dependencyDashboardHeader: Routine updates target dev and require review plus full cross-platform CI. Node tracks the newest officially promoted LTS line, never Current, and its synchronized runtime/archive pins require qualification before merge. Yarn, Effect, provider SDKs, native packaging and security resolutions stay on the manual audited path. Check GitHub Dependabot alerts separately for excluded dependencies and main; an empty dashboard is not security clearance. See docs/dependency-updates.md.
prBodyNotes: Human review and all applicable Linux/macOS/Windows quality and native artifact checks are required; do not merge a failed or incomplete update.
Provider, patched Effect, native-runtime, toolchain and security-resolution upgrades require the manual audits documented in AGENTS.md and docs/dependency-updates.md.

Node.js LTS proposals must keep .node-version, mise, package engines, declarations and reviewed Windows archive hashes synchronized. Never substitute Current, guess LTS from an even major, or merge an unqualified runtime.

packageRules.description: Follow the newest officially promoted Node LTS using Renovate's release-schedule-aware Node versioning, not the npm Current tag or a frozen major.
Keep declarations on an officially promoted Node LTS major too, while retaining the normal npm package-age gate and human review.
The mise manager is admitted only to synchronize Node; future non-Node tools remain manual rather than expanding the runtime/toolchain surface.
Keep matching React runtime and type packages together without combining unrelated upgrades.
Keep the Vite compiler and its integration packages aligned.
The Vitest runner, coverage and browser integration share version-sensitive interfaces.
Keep lint/format executables and their plugin API in one reviewable tooling change.
Pin action code to immutable commits; action updates remain proposals, never automatic merges.
Major API changes need dashboard approval before a branch/PR is created, then normal human review and CI.
Security resolutions are deliberate overrides, not ordinary version pins; changing or relaxing them requires a separate audit.
Effect prereleases and the version-bound RPC patch must move atomically after a manual patch rebase and compatibility audit.
Provider SDKs require protocol, token/lifecycle and package-integrity audits; Claude also requires its complete-package age/signature review.
Native and desktop packaging dependencies require audited, synchronized source/staged pins and native qualification.
Yarn remains an exact, manually qualified repository-wide policy; Node has its separate synchronized latest-LTS proposal rule.
